questions: Inspect Qwen headless JSON, approvals, safe read-only execution and session persistence.
Compare budget, cancellation and resume contracts without assuming Claude-compatible flags.
decision: Treat Qwen headless JSON, budgets and permissions as its own tested protocol, not a Claude-compatible shell command.
code_observations: The Qwen adapter currently constructs a headless invocation with configured approval/safe-mode controls and a report schema.
Provider documentation distinguishes JSON/stream output, session persistence and budget exhaustion; those distinctions must survive normalization in the shared runner.
implementation_steps: Add version/help fixtures for supported Qwen CLI releases and explicit format selection. Keep JSON-array output and streaming JSONL parsing separate.
Normalize terminal result, tool activity, budget exhaustion, quota and transport errors without treating any intermediate assistant message as completion.
Qualify read-only operation with supported tool exclusions and sandbox controls. Yolo/approval automation alone must not authorize a supposedly read-only observer.
Capture resumable session identifiers only if explicitly enabled and retention is documented. Otherwise keep fresh-worker behavior and artifact handoff.
Apply the shared bounded output spool and process-tree cancellation contract rather than maintaining a second unbounded capture implementation.
proposed_acceptance_tests: Replay JSON and JSONL fixtures with interleaved tool messages, malformed records and missing terminal results.
Budget/turn exhaustion is recorded separately from semantic failure and transient availability.
A read-only fake/qualified command cannot select shell/write/edit tools outside the allowlist.
Large output is drained without deadlock; cancellation stops owned descendants.
Unsupported schema or sandbox flags fail closed with an actionable version reason.

alternatives.title: One command template for all versions
alternatives.tradeoff: Low code volume but hides incompatible output and permission changes.

alternatives.title: Small Qwen-specific contract and shared safe process infrastructure
alternatives.tradeoff: Reuses common safety while respecting vendor semantics.

alternatives.title: Parse the last arbitrary JSON object as success
alternatives.tradeoff: May accept a tool event or partial output that never satisfied the task.

cost_model: Use local fixtures for routine protocol regression and only bounded authorized live smoke tests for upgrades. No extra diagnostic model is needed for known exit/error classes.
unverified: The installed Qwen release and its actual exit-code behavior were not exercised. Published budget codes must be pinned before becoming authoritative classifications.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated model calls; tests listed here are implementation obligations, not claimed passes.
